intro.sounan.1: November 2nd, 4:40 p.m. — the trail down Kaerazu-yama
intro.sounan.3: Someone called. You stepped off the trail.
item.sounan.battery.desc: Right-click to put fresh batteries in the flashlight.
item.sounan.bear_bell.desc: Right-click to ring. The peeking things hate it, the one behind you lets go. It is loud.
item.sounan.flare.desc: Right-click to ignite: forty seconds of red fire. The mountain hates fire.
item.sounan.flashlight.desc: Right-click to switch on/off. The batteries drain. Some things must not be lit.
item.sounan.memo.desc: A note you found. Read it again in the phone's notes (J).
item.sounan.omamori.desc: Your grandmother's charm. It takes your place, once.
item.sounan.omiki.desc: Sake to offer at a shrine.
item.sounan.phone.desc: Right-click (or P) to open. Sneak + right-click: torch. No signal.
item.sounan.rope.desc: Tie it to the climbers' stake at the cliff to climb down.
item.sounan.trail_map.desc: Right-click to unfold. Wet, torn at one edge.
note.sounan.1.body:
October 28th. On the way down someone called me. "Hey! Over here!" I thought it was a rescuer, so I left the trail.
That was the mistake.

There is no trail here. Only the sound of the stream.

— Saeki
note.sounan.1.title: Torn page from a wet notebook
note.sounan.10.body:
1987.10.3 Rain. Someone already here, asleep at the back. Left quietly.

1993.11.2 The key is for the old tunnel gate, I think. Someone take it.

1998.10.29 Saeki. Something is sleeping at the back. Its breath is wet. Taking the key. Don't wake it. Crouch.

2011.8.15 (the handwriting shakes too much to read)

2026.11.3 %1$s - made it this far.
note.sounan.10.title: Hikers' logbook
note.sounan.11.body:
There is signal here. I called home. My wife answered.
She was crying, asking where I was. I told her the mountain's name.

Then, on the line, she said:
"You don't have to come back. You could just stay there forever."

It wasn't her voice.
note.sounan.11.title: Under the pylon
note.sounan.12.body:
At the far end of the tunnel I can see the light of the exit.
But however far I walk, it gets no closer.

Behind me, something huge is crawling on all fours.

Fire. Light a fire. The mountain hates fire—
note.sounan.12.title: The exit
note.sounan.13.body:
Kaerino district association
Anyone entering Kaerazu-yama at night must keep these rules.

I. If someone carrying a light calls you on the mountain at night, never follow.

II. Never meet the eyes of what peeks from behind the trees. Never shine a light on it.

III. If you feel something at your back, never turn around. Keep walking.

IV. Never wake the master of a hut. Make no sound inside, and crouch.

V. Whoever passes the shrine must offer sake. Those who do not lose their way in the fog.

VI. If you meet Oyama-sama, light a fire. Oyama-sama hates fire.

Those the mountain calls do not come back.
note.sounan.13.title: Kaerazu-yama: rules for entering the mountain
note.sounan.14.body:
Those who disappeared on Kaerazu-yama

October 1987 (covered in moss)
November 1993 (likewise)
October 1998 - Kazuya Saeki
August 2011 (the name has been scratched off)
November 2026 - %1$s

- may they rest in peace
note.sounan.14.title: In memory of the lost
note.sounan.2.body:
Follow a stream downhill and you reach a village. That is what they teach you.
But this stream seems to lead deeper into the mountain.

Someone behind me walks in step with me.
I don't dare look back.
note.sounan.2.title: Scribbled by the stream
note.sounan.3.body:
The climbers' stake is old but it holds. Once down, there is no climbing back.

When I reached the bottom someone was looking down at me from the top.
It had my face.
note.sounan.3.title: Scrap below the cliff
note.sounan.4.body:
I am following the pink marking tapes. Old ones, new ones.

Who tied the new ones?
There should be no one on this mountain but me.

There was a tape tied around my wrist.
When?
note.sounan.4.title: About the tapes
note.sounan.5.body:
I should not have followed the tapes. The path ends here.

Shoes are lined up at the foot of the tree. Neatly, in pairs. Many pairs.

Will mine be set here too?
note.sounan.5.title: Dead end
note.sounan.6.body:
Something peeks from behind the trees. Head tilted, one eye.
When I shone my light on it, it smiled. So I don't anymore. I don't meet its eye.

If I don't go near, it does nothing.
...so far.
note.sounan.6.title: Watched
note.sounan.7.body:
"The mountain people" - Haruka Yamada, 3rd grade

Grandma said if something calls your name on the mountain at night, don't answer.
If someone with a light calls you, don't follow.

The mountain people are lonely, so they take you with them.
note.sounan.7.title: A child's composition
note.sounan.8.body:
Everyone in this village was called into the mountain.
The old ones first. Then the children. My husband went out after someone with a light and never came back.

Tonight it is my turn. Outside, my husband's voice is calling my name.
I must not answer. I must not—
note.sounan.8.title: The last villager
note.sounan.9.body:
Beyond the shrine the fog never clears. However far I walk, I end up back at the shrine.

I remembered the village rule:
"Whoever passes the shrine must offer sake."

There was sake left in one of the houses.
...something sleeps in that house.
note.sounan.9.title: About the shrine
phone.sounan.call.hint: Calls only work where there is signal
phone.sounan.msg.kenta.1: Kaerazu-yama, seriously? The locals say never go up there at night.
phone.sounan.msg.kenta.3: If something calls your name, don't answer. I mean it.
phone.sounan.msg.kenta.4: Hey, you okay? Your mom called me.
phone.sounan.msg.kenta.5: Driving up now. I'll wait at the trailhead.
phone.sounan.msg.kenta.6: Your car's still at the trailhead. I'm sorry. I should have stopped you.
phone.sounan.msg.kenta.7: I'm getting married. I wish you could come.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.1: You're going up Kaerazu-yama tomorrow? Be careful.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.10: I tidied your room a little today. I'm sorry.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.11: Three years now. I called your name toward the mountain again today. You never answer.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.2: It's a day hike. I'll be down by evening.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.3: Have a good hike. Text me when you're down.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.6: I called the police. Answer me.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.8: A search team went up this morning. Please, answer.
phone.sounan.msg.mom.9: They called off the search. But I'm still waiting.
phone.sounan.msg.work.1: Where are the slides for tomorrow's meeting?
phone.sounan.msg.work.2: Your family told us. Don't worry about work...

thought.sounan.bag: There it is...! It must have rolled down when I fell.
thought.sounan.fall: ...! A fall like that would kill me.
thought.sounan.flash_low: The light is dimming... the batteries won't last.
thought.sounan.fog: The fog is too thick... I can't see anything.
thought.sounan.hokora: An old shrine. If only I had something to offer...
thought.sounan.hokora_done: The fog has cleared. I can get through.
thought.sounan.hokora_need: I need to offer sake... there was some in the village.
thought.sounan.key: A key... the tag says "Old Tunnel".
thought.sounan.locked: Chained and padlocked. I need a key.
thought.sounan.need_rope: An old stake. With a rope I could climb down here.
thought.sounan.old_bag: ...not mine. An old bag, long empty.
thought.sounan.omiki: Sake... an offering. Maybe for a shrine.
thought.sounan.roped: Rope tied. I can climb down now.
thought.sounan.tunnel: Pitch black... no sign of the exit.
thought.sounan.ushiro: ...I feel I must not look back.
thought.sounan.wake: ...ugh. Where... am I? My bag is gone.
thought.sounan.wake_3: How many days...? The date on the phone is wrong.
thought.sounan.wake_4: I can barely remember who I was...
